Top Top 12 Takeaways from the KDIGO 2025
Clinical Practice Guideline for the
12 Management of IgA Nephropathy
Diagnosis of IgA nephropathy (IgAN)
biomarkers for the diagnosis. To ensure an early diagnosis and prompt treatment, a kidney biopsy
1 IgAN can only be diagnosed with a kidney biopsy, as there are no validated serum or urine
should be considered in all adults with proteinuria ≥0.5 g/d (or equivalent) in whom IgAN is a
possible diagnosis (Figure 1).
Prognosis
IgA-dominant
Clinical and histologic data at the time of kidney biopsy can be used for risk stratification by the
Prediction Tools nor the Oxford Classification MEST-C score should be used to decide on a specific
2 International IgAN Prediction Tools (Figure 1). However, neither the International IgAN glomerulonephritis
therapy. There are no validated prognostic serum or urine biomarkers other than eGFR and
proteinuria. Consider secondary causes:
• IgA vasculitis
• IgA nephropathy secondary to:
Treatment goals in patients with IgAN at risk of progressive loss - Viral infection (HIV, hepatitis) Treat primary
of kidney function - Inflammatory bowel disease process
- Autoimmune disease
The treatment goal in patients with IgAN at risk of progressive loss of kidney function (i.e., - Liver cirrhosis
proteinuria ≥0.5 g/d [or equivalent] while on or off treatment) is to reduce the rate of loss of • IgA-dominant infection-related GN
kidney function to the physiological state (i.e., <1 ml/min/yr for most adults) for the rest of the
patient’s life. Currently, the only validated early biomarker to help guide clinical decision-making
3 Idiopathic IgAN
is urine protein excretion, which should be maintained at a minimum of <0.5 g/d (or equivalent),
and ideally at <0.3 g/d (or equivalent).
Focus of the management of patients with IgAN who Score the kidney biopsy
are at risk of progressive loss of kidney function using the MEST-C score
The focus of the management in most patients should be tosimultaneously: i) prevent or reduce
4 IgA-IC formation and IgA-IC–mediated glomerular injury (whether this requires lifelong or Quantify progression risk at diagnosis using
intermittent therapy is currently unknown) and ii) manage the consequences of existing the International IgAN Prediction Tool to
IgAN-induced nephron loss (likely lifelong). inform discussions with patients for
shared decision-making
Managing the consequences of IgAN-induced nephron loss
All patients should receive extensive lifestyle advice on smoking and vaping cessation, weight Enroll the patient in a disease registry,
control, dietary sodium restriction (<2 g/d), and regular exercise. Blood pressure should be if one is available
controlled to a target of ≤120/70 mm Hg.
5 Patients and their caregivers should be provided
Managing the IgAN-specific drivers of nephron loss (Figure 2) information on national and international patient
A 9-month course of Nefecon is suggested for patients with IgAN who are at risk of progressive advocacy organizations for disease management
loss of kidney function. Where Nefecon is not available, patients should be treated with a education and peer support
Tonsillectomy alone or with pulsed glucocorticoids is recommended by the Japanese Society of
6 reduced-dose systemic glucocorticoid regimen combined with antimicrobial prophylaxis. Figure 1
Nephrology for the treatment of patients with IgAN, but it should not be performed as a
treatment of IgAN in non-Japanese patients. Similarly, in Chinese patients in whom glucocorti-
coids are being considered, MMF may be used as a glucocorticoid-sparing agent.

kidney function loss
